components.description: The integral of a nonnegative simple function
components.source_comparison: Durrett p. 18, Step 1: simple functions with real coefficients on disjoint sets of finite measure under a sigma-finite mu; representation not unique but the definition consistent. Handbook: nonnegative partition form on an arbitrary measure space with the 0 times infinity convention worked (body 26-43); consistency proved in the next entry; the sigma-finite setting and the signed finite-measure stage are identified and proved to agree (body 11-16, 172-195; annex 244-250).

components.description: Simple integrals and refinement
components.source_comparison: Durrett Lemma 1.4.1 (i)-(iii) with the common-refinement proof (p. 19) and Lemma 1.4.2 (iv)-(vi): well-definedness, additivity, scaling, monotonicity, indicator and overlapping-sum formulas proved in full (annex 12-47); the a.e. and signed-scalar forms are supplied at the general level (body 102-108, 151-170), which contains the signed simple functions of Durrett's stage.

components.description: The nonnegative integral and almost-everywhere statements
components.source_comparison: Durrett p. 18 (a.e. definition), p. 21 (int_E f = int f 1_E; Step 3 supremum over bounded h with finite-measure positive region, Lemma 1.4.4): supplied; the simple-function supremum is proved equal to Durrett's Step 3 class on sigma-finite exhaustions (body 183-194; annex 233-242).

components.description: Monotone convergence
components.source_comparison: Durrett Thm 1.5.7 (p. 27) and Thm 1.6.6 (p. 30): stated and proved directly (a declared variant of Durrett's route through Fatou, body 13-15). Exercises 1.5.5 (p. 28) and 1.6.13 (p. 37), which replace the hypothesis f_n >= 0: absent from the route.
components.gap: Partial: the source variant that weakens the hypothesis of monotone convergence is not supplied on the route. Durrett, Exercise 1.5.5 (p. 28) and Exercise 1.6.13 (p. 37), replace f_n >= 0 by an integrable negative part of the first term: if g_n increases to g and the integral of g_1^- is finite, the integrals of g_n increase to the integral of g (for expectations: E X_1^- finite and X_n increasing to X give E X_n increasing to E X). The route states only the nonnegative theorem (integration-expectation body 81-90, a.e. form 107-108) and the counterexample r_n = -1_[n,infinity) (body 260-262), which shows that monotonicity alone fails but not what replaces nonnegativity. Text addressing it exists only in the unrouted handbook/parts/p15/measure-integration-and-product-constructions-w02c-p15-005.tex (thm:p15-w02c-p15-005-monotone-lower, lines 60-71). Not assessed here because it is not on the route.

components.gap: Partial: the source variant of term-by-term integration for signed functions is not supplied on the route. Durrett, Exercise 1.5.10 (p. 28), replaces the hypothesis f_n >= 0 of the series formula (Exercise 1.5.6; body 99) by finiteness of the sum over n of the integrals of |f_n|, and concludes that the sum of the integrals of f_n equals the integral of the sum. components.gap: Partial: Durrett's notation for the special cases of the integral, stated after Theorem 1.4.7 (pp. 23-24), is not supplied on the route: (a) int f(x) dx for the integral against Lebesgue measure on R^d; (b) int_a^b f(x) dx for the integral over E = [a,b]; (c) int f(x) dG(x) for the measure with mu((a,b]) = G(b) - G(a), where the route defines dG only for a probability distribution function (convolution-gamma-normal.tex 102-104); (d) the sum over i in Omega of f(i) for the integral against counting measure on a countable set, with Durrett's remark that results for sums follow from those for integrals, where the route has only the probability-mass sum of the expectation theorem (body 344-347).
